Calculate the bending stress distribution across a rectangular beam cross-section using the linear-elastic flexure formula.
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The second moment of area about the neutral axis is I = bh³/12 = 50 × 120³ / 12 = 7 200 000 mm⁴.
The internal bending moment in the section is M = 4 000 000 N·mm, sagging (positive by convention).
The transverse coordinate y is measured from the neutral axis (centroid), positive upward.
Use the governing relation σ = −M·y / I, which yields compression (σ < 0) on the top fiber and tension (σ > 0) on the bottom fiber under a sagging moment.
Evaluate σ at three locations: the neutral axis y = 0 mm, the top fiber y = +h/2 = +60 mm, and the bottom fiber y = −h/2 = −60 mm.
Report results in MPa (1 MPa = 1 N/mm²), consistent with the N–mm–MPa unit system.
Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic material behavior (Euler-Bernoulli beam theory): plane sections remain plane and perpendicular to the neutral axis, stresses vary linearly through the depth, and no axial force or transverse shear effect is superimposed.
